profiles.title: CMU/Pitt: flexible recording shank with two chemical sites
profiles.summary: A flexible shank carries 16 recording contacts plus two independently wired chemical-release sites. The two larger sites are not extra recording channels. The virtual route ends at electrical testing and an inert payload proxy, not delivery to tissue.

variants.label: 16 electrical measurement sites
variants.description: Small Pt/Au/Pt contacts have a PEDOT:PSS sensing finish. The larger sites are addressed separately.

variants.label: 2 chemical-site interfaces
variants.description: The paper used different payload-loaded coatings; the atlas represents them by identity and finite inventory, not actuating or preparing biological payloads.

variants.label: Pressure-driven perfusion channel
variants.description: Not this probe: its local coating has finite capacity, not a pump, microchannel or refillable reservoir.

steps.title: Create the compliant base
steps.detail: Use a silicon carrier and lower Parylene-C film; reflectometry tracks film thickness separately from later top passivation.
steps.check: Confirm the lower film is present before metal; it is not a sacrificial layer.

steps.title: Pattern the shared metal stack
steps.detail: Lift-off defines a Pt/Au/Pt sandwich with thin narrower recording leads and separate wider chemical-site connections. Match the 18 functional nets to the backend and preserve the unused connector pad.
steps.check: A reconstruction with 18 acquisition channels fails. Test each of the two large nets separately from the 16 small ones.

steps.title: Open upper windows, then separate the perimeter
steps.detail: A second nominal 10 µm Parylene-C film covers the routes. The first oxygen plasma etch opens metal windows and starts the outline; a second outline mask defines the remaining thickness.
steps.check: Hole over a site: stops at metal. Perimeter outside the site: clears the two films. Verify these endpoints independently.

steps.title: Release and register the flat-cable connection
steps.detail: The authors exploit weak adhesion in water rather than dissolving a deliberately deposited sacrificial metal. Anneal the detached film on a flat support and link the flat cable to the adapter PCB.
steps.check: A 19-position ZIF is not 19 populated signal contacts; check the documented vacant position.

steps.title: Treat the contacts according to role
steps.detail: On recording sites, the conducting polymer finish changes interface impedance. Chemical sites use a different particle-containing polymer coating in the source; payload preparation and actuation are not part of this bench workflow.
steps.check: Preserve a bare-vs-coated recording-site comparison. Test a finite, inert inventory proxy separately without equating impedance with delivered quantity.

steps.title: Test an instrumented dummy load
steps.detail: Drive the recording input with a calibration tone. Model the two auxiliary lines as electrical loads and show where actuation artifacts would mask recording, with no active compound or biological output.
steps.check: Mark the artifact interval unreadable rather than computing changes in firing through it.

gaps: No clinical dosing, preparation or release instructions, loaded compounds, or tissue experiments are part of the virtual workflow.
Published changes in impedance and finite coating behavior are distinct measurements, not universal thresholds.

sources.title: Malekoshoaraie, Wu et al. (2024): fully flexible recording/release probes
sources.note: Figures 1, 6 and 7 and fabrication Methods describe the two-mask polymer etch, weak-adhesion release, connector and distinct recording and payload coatings.

profiles.title: NeuroString: laser-converted porous conductor in elastomer
profiles.summary: The electrode is a cut cross-section of a conductive nanoparticle/graphene network in elastomer. Making a long, conductive fiber would not by itself reproduce its selective electrochemical response.

variants.label: Short, multi-string layout
variants.description: The studied brain assembly shows three measurement channels. A 3–5 mm device segment is distinct from tip width and thickness.

variants.label: Long, compliant layout
variants.description: A separate tens-to-hundreds-of-millimeters layout is used for the gut; the authors pattern individual traces and evaluate movement effects.

variants.label: Use generic extracellular spike readout
variants.description: This device senses chemical concentration using electrochemical measurements, not action-potential voltage.

steps.title: Define separate sensor layouts and feedstock
steps.detail: Prepare a film on a PI carrier using a qualified metalloporphyrin-containing polymer precursor. Fe- and Ni-containing precursors lead to different oxide particles; do not substitute a bare commercial PI sheet silently.
steps.check: Keep film batch, catalyst identity and geometry traceable through transfer.

steps.title: Convert the patterned film to a porous conductor
steps.detail: The study uses a CO₂ laser engraver to carbonize the precursor. This is a material transformation, not photolithographic UV resist exposure; the register has no qualified matching engraver.
steps.check: Use Raman/microscopy and continuity on a processed witness, not a dark color alone, to identify a conductive region.

steps.title: Embed, release and flip the composite
steps.detail: SEBS penetrates the graphene network, enabling peel and transfer. Encapsulate from the second face while retaining backend contact access.
steps.check: Compare resistance before and after transfer. A torn conductor can sit inside an intact-looking elastomer strip.

steps.title: Separate the geometry appropriate to the branch
steps.detail: For the short version, the paper isolates individual narrow strings; the longer layout has separately patterned conductors. The cutting operation is not interchangeable with earlier laser carbonization.
steps.check: Inspect edge isolation and continuity at bent and unloaded states; do not use one unstretched measurement as a fatigue qualification.

steps.title: Open the sensing cross-section
steps.detail: The cut end surface rather than the sidewall is the working face. Oxygen plasma and a Nafion finish are used in the reported sensor; retain the insulator along non-sensing regions.
steps.check: Distinguish a deliberately exposed end from accidental sidewall damage by imaging and blank measurements.

steps.title: Calibrate a chemical signal with motion controls
steps.detail: Compare blank and known calibration standards, reference electrode and stretched/unstrained states. The exact fast-scan waveform bandwidth requires a qualified test chain beyond a generic instrument listing.
steps.check: A current peak in a mixed sample does not prove one specific neurotransmitter. Store concentration, current, reference, strain and interference conditions separately.

gaps: No registered CO₂ conversion/cutting station or verified fast-scan acquisition bandwidth has been identified.
An elastomer end-face model is not a biological selectivity, chronic lifetime or drug-response predictor.

sources.title: Li et al. (2022): a tissue-like neurotransmitter sensor
sources.note: Methods and Extended Data Figure 1 distinguish graphene/metal-oxide laser conversion, brain vs gut layouts, SEBS transfer, end face and calibration. Detecting catecholamines need not uniquely identify dopamine.

profiles.title: SIAT: aligned MXene / PEDOT:PSS wet-spun fibers
profiles.summary: These are conductive Ti₃C₂ titanium carbide sheets assembled into fibers; the composite also contains PEDOT:PSS. Wet coagulation with mechanical take-up is not electrospinning or thermal drawing.

variants.label: MX: pure MXene
variants.description: Use the non-composite fiber as a separate material comparator.

variants.label: MPP: composite fiber
variants.description: Published approximately 30 µm composite fibers incorporate the conductive polymer between oriented sheets.

variants.label: Produce it on an electrospinner
variants.description: An electric-field jet is not the paper’s two-step wet coagulation route; the register’s electrospinner cannot be assumed compatible.

steps.title: Lock the flake material and dispersion
steps.detail: Treat qualified Ti₃C₂ flakes and the selected dispersion as inputs. Mechanically dispersing any conductive powder is not evidence for liquid-crystalline order.
steps.check: Record precursor identity and polymer presence; support any ordering claim with structural evidence.

steps.title: Form and consolidate the fiber
steps.detail: The authors describe shear alignment followed by initial coagulation and a strain-controlled second solidification. The register has a pump concept but does not document the complete spinning and take-up line.
steps.check: Track breaks, diameter and take-up alignment as separate outcomes. Without the coupled line, mark fiber production external.

steps.title: Inspect longitudinal and transverse structure
steps.detail: Use microscopy of fiber and cross-section to distinguish intersheet network morphology from a surface coating. A cross-section is also needed to estimate a conduction area.
steps.check: Measure area/diameter rather than assuming a perfect circular 30 µm section for every specimen.

steps.title: Separate the exposed interface from the lead
steps.detail: Represent a defined exposed end and insulated connection on a bench coupon. The publicly checked summaries do not establish one uniform package/insulation design across skin and implanted variants.
steps.check: Keep exposed geometric area, immersed length and end contact method with the test record.

steps.title: Compare conductivity and interface response
steps.detail: Measure longitudinal resistance versus length on the fiber; measure frequency-dependent impedance at the electrolyte interface on a defined area. They do not share units or identify the same failure.
steps.check: Do not convert an area-normalized quantity to raw ohms without its area and convention, or interpret charge storage as charge injection.

gaps: The complete wet-spinning take-up fixture, process calibration and exact channelized packaging remain external.
An electrical test of the material does not predict efficacy, tissue stimulation, or chronic durability.

sources.title: Gou et al. (2025): microscale MXene/PEDOT-PSS fiber electrodes
sources.note: Primary publication identifies Ti₃C₂, a two-step wet-spinning route, the composite and approximately 30 µm fibers. Electrical characterization applies to the particular material and test geometry.

sources.title: SIAT: liquid-crystal MXene fiber process (Chinese)
sources.note: Investigators’ institutional account describes shear-aligned flakes, coagulation followed by strain-controlled solidification, and pure MXene versus composite fibers.

profiles.title: CIBR USEs: eight flexible ribbons and a common central anchor
profiles.summary: This umbrella is fabricated flat and becomes three-dimensional by folding. Its eight ribbons and shared central reference do not imply eight recording channels. The 120- and 240-channel versions change geometry and connector count.

variants.label: 120-channel layout
variants.description: 38 µm ribbon width, 50 µm site pitch and one 120-channel FPC in the publication.

variants.label: 240-channel layout
variants.description: 70 µm ribbon width, 30 µm site pitch and two 120-channel FPCs.

variants.label: Pt or PEDOT:PSS contact finishes
variants.description: Two reported finishes; preserve the selected material and its comparison instead of combining them into one default coating.

steps.title: Lay out eight ribbons on a temporary wafer
steps.detail: Start from a patterned Al release film on a 4-inch Si carrier. The geometry has serpentine stretch sections, straight recording regions and a 210 µm shared central reference.
steps.check: Check location of central reference and each site; do not mistake ten or six designs per wafer for a percentage yield.

steps.title: Build the two-metal, three-insulator routing stack
steps.detail: PI separates two patterned Cr/Au layers. Imaging or sectioning can inspect the cross-section; independent continuity tests are needed for two-level routes.
steps.check: Report an open route and an adjacent-layer short separately; include the minimum-width region in inspection.

steps.title: Pattern umbrella boundaries and strengthen the hub
steps.detail: Use oxygen RIE for the polymer outline, then form I/O pads and localized SU-8 reinforcement at the hub/ribbon junctions. A uniform rigid coating would change the stretch mechanism.
steps.check: Hub reinforcement must not immobilize the serpentine spans or cover recording sites.

steps.title: Bond FPCs before dissolving the release layer
steps.detail: After separation into carrier pieces, ACF flip-chip attachment joins the I/O region to one or two 120-channel FPCs. Remove the Al layer only after this supported connection.
steps.check: Use one FPC for the 120-channel variant and two for 240; check nets under the actual ACF interface.

steps.title: Finish, support and mechanically screen
steps.detail: Electrodeposit Pt or PEDOT:PSS, then temporarily support the flexible recording area. A safe virtual/inert phantom test moves the central hub and tracks continuity in all eight ribbons.
steps.check: A central-reference open can invalidate recording with intact signal traces; a single torn ribbon is spatially distinct.

gaps: No recovered full mask files, lot-wide yield, qualified ACF bonding head or validated mechanical fatigue model are implied.
A folding/continuity demonstration on an inert fixture is not validation of surgical deployment or long-term recording.

sources.title: Bai et al. (2026): umbrella-type stretchable probes
sources.note: Figure 1 and Methods describe two routings, three PI layers, two Cr/Au levels, SU-8 reinforcement, assembly before release and the agarose mechanical reference.

profiles.title: Fudan MNIS: flexible, dielectrically isolated transistor and optical array
profiles.summary: The same silicon transistor structure can sense capacitively coupled signals or light, depending on bias. A separate gold resistive element measures temperature. The buried oxide retained from the SOI supplier becomes the outward-facing barrier; it is not the deposited transistor gate dielectric.

variants.label: Electrical pickup through intact oxide
variants.description: The transistor reads a capacitively coupled input; no exposed-metal recording window is needed.

variants.label: Photodetection mode
variants.description: The same active semiconductor changes its response under illumination; this does not add a microLED emitter to the wafer.

variants.label: Gold resistance thermometer
variants.description: The metal resistor is a separate temperature transducer on the same flexible device, not a third operating mode of the transistor.

steps.title: Prepare the SOI donor and diffusion mask
steps.detail: The reported donor has 220 nm device silicon, a 300 nm buried oxide and a 500 µm handle thinned to 200 µm. Deposit and open a separate PECVD silicon-oxide masking film. Only its exposed regions will take the dopant.
steps.check: Record device-silicon, BOX and handle thickness independently; a thick diffusion mask does not change the BOX barrier.

steps.title: Form source/drain regions and isolate active islands
steps.detail: The published route uses boron predeposition and drive-in in a dedicated tube furnace, then patterned silicon isolation trenches. A general box furnace is not a qualified dopant line.
steps.check: Track actual doping history and active-island isolation. Treat unqualified wafer diffusion as a blocked external module, not an assumed material.

steps.title: Build the gate and interconnect stack
steps.detail: Deposit the 50 nm PECVD SiO₂ and 15 nm ALD Al₂O₃ gate insulators. Open source/drain contacts and sputter patterned Cr/Au for interconnects, gate metallization and thermal resistance.
steps.check: Compare transistor transfer and output curves to controls for gate leakage and contact failure. A working Au thermometer does not establish transistor action.

steps.title: Support the electronics before removing the handle
steps.detail: Passivate with PI and laminate the front to a supported assembly incorporating 15 µm Kapton and PDMS. The reported finished flexible stack is about 31 µm, not 31 µm of silicon.
steps.check: Check axis and handling orientation: the BOX is exposed from the handle side after transfer.

steps.title: Expose, but do not open, the buried oxide
steps.detail: The authors remove most of the handle by ICP-RIE and finish selectively with XeF₂ vapor. A reactive-ion chamber or wet bench is not a verified substitute for the missing XeF₂ station; the completed release remains external.
steps.check: Verify silicon clearance and integrity of the outward-facing thermal oxide, including edge regions, before accepting the capacitive-sensing interface.

steps.title: Separate test modes and interconnects
steps.detail: Use the 4 × 4 transistor array with its recorded site map. Test electrical response with a known capacitively coupled signal, light response using a measured optical input against a dark trace, and Au resistance against a temperature standard.
steps.check: Record electrical gain, photocurrent and resistance-versus-temperature in separate units. Do not infer on-chip multiplexing or 16 thermometers from 16 transistors.

steps.title: Characterize barrier integrity under load
steps.detail: Use defined bends or soak conditions and compare electrical leakage and sensitivity before and after. The accelerated experiment was run at 70 °C; this is not a measured lifetime in a person.
steps.check: Keep lost contact, cracked barrier and ordinary thermal response distinguishable. No time-to-clinical-failure conversion is supplied.

gaps: No instrumented boron diffusion line, XeF₂ module or transferable full foundry control plan is established by this equipment register.
Actual die exposure requires an appropriately sized holder. Published bending and accelerated aging cannot certify long-term barrier performance.

sources.title: Li et al.: active multimodal neural interface (MNIS)
sources.note: Experimental Section and Figure S1 separate donor SOI, doped active islands, gate dielectric, support and removal of the handle. Figure 1 shows 16 PMOS devices and Au thermometry; Figure 3 separates operating modes.

profiles.title: SIAT LIG: bilateral strain sensor or polymer–gold neural electrode
profiles.summary: These are two different devices that can share acquisition time, not two measurements from the same contact. One turns mechanical deformation into resistance change; the other reduces the impedance of an electrode–electrolyte interface.

variants.label: BiL-LIG mechanical sensor
variants.description: Bilateral rather than single-sided conductors change the strain-response curve. The reported range improvement is relative to the reference, not a claim of 40% absolute usable strain.

variants.label: IntE-LIG electrode array
variants.description: The conductive polymer–gold finish modifies a LIG electrical interface. A low impedance ratio is not evidence of mechanical sensing.

variants.label: PEMS: common acquisition timeline
variants.description: The study combines the two devices. Time alignment and individual channel calibration remain necessary for multimodal output.

steps.title: Choose the output domain and controls
steps.detail: For mechanical readout retain an identically defined single-layer control. For electrode readout retain unmodified LIG contacts of the same exposed geometry. The two controls cannot substitute for one another.
steps.check: A change in strain produces a resistance ratio; electrode impedance is complex and frequency dependent. Label each data field accordingly.

steps.title: Form the laser-defined conductors externally
steps.detail: The researchers report laser-induced graphene, not laser-exposed resist. A wavelength, substrate, atmosphere and qualified conversion line were not established from the materials reviewed. Do not import the NeuroString precursor or assume the registered MLA can make LIG.
steps.check: Require a defined conversion process and witness characterization. A visible dark mark alone does not prove a functional graphene network.

steps.title: Mechanical branch: compare one and two sides
steps.detail: Measure resistance while applying controlled deformation in the same geometry. The reported high-strain gauge factor is 3.77; it is dimensionless, local to its stated strain regime, not a universal low-strain specification.
steps.check: Fit the slope of fractional resistance change against strain over a stated window. Compare loading and unloading, baseline drift and practical working range separately.

steps.title: Electrode branch: qualify the modified surface
steps.detail: The institution reports a conductive polymer–gold composite layer on LIG. The public evidence reviewed does not establish the layer order or a compatible local deposition recipe, so local processing is not claimed.
steps.check: Distinguish the integrated composite from an assumed Au film or untreated LIG; document panel, area and comparator before testing.

steps.title: Measure the interfacial response, not DC trace resistance
steps.detail: Compare modified and unmodified surfaces with the same electrolyte, reference, area and frequency. The study reports up to a 98.5% relative impedance reduction at 1 kHz, not 98.5 Ω or a universal cutoff.
steps.check: Calculate the ratio from the two matched measurements and retain the spectrum; a DC continuity test cannot produce the same quantity.

steps.title: Synchronize two fixture outputs
steps.detail: Pair mechanical motion on a dummy fixture with a separately tagged electrical input. Store the channels, units and clocks distinctly before aligning them on a shared timeline.
steps.check: Recover independently imposed event offsets. Cross-correlation is not evidence of a physiological or causal relationship.

gaps: No exact laser workcell, process window, coating chemistry or production yield is established by the verified public material.
The bench route reproduces neither experiments on living subjects nor seizure detection, diagnosis or treatment.

sources.title: Liao et al. (2026): laser-induced graphene for multimodal monitoring
sources.note: The primary article identifies the two device branches, the single-layer comparator, multimodal system and relative rather than absolute performance figures.

sources.title: SIAT: bilateral strain sensor and engineered LIG electrode (Chinese)
sources.note: Research group describes bilateral structures, conductive-polymer/gold composite treatment, and 1 kHz impedance comparison. No calibrated laser or full layer recipe is established here.

profiles.title: TUM: four Blackrock 8 × 8 arrays on one pedestal
profiles.summary: The hand-interface catalog entry is a 256-electrode assembly: four 64-electrode arrays, one cable bundle per array and one shared titanium pedestal. It is not a new 256-site lithographic die and not four standard 96-channel implants.

variants.label: Documented TUM hardware: 4 × 64
variants.description: Each 8 × 8 grid carries 64 iridium-oxide-coated 1.5 mm silicon needles. Four grids have separate physical positions.

variants.label: Single-grid fixture for fault isolation
variants.description: A synthetic reference can exercise one 64-site block at a time. It does not convert the purchased assembly into four independent products.

variants.label: Four 10 × 10 arrays or four 96-channel maps
variants.description: Reject for this configuration even though such sizes occur elsewhere in the Utah family.

steps.title: Specify all four grids and the shared output
steps.detail: Use the four-array hardware shown in Figure 1. A grid coordinate is not a globally unique channel without an array ID. Record architecture separately from the historical clinical context.
steps.check: Four arrays × eight rows × eight columns = 256 distinct physical electrodes. Never reuse a 96-channel map to pad the count.

steps.title: Treat the commercial array fabrication as external
steps.detail: The investigators identify Blackrock Utah/NeuroPort hardware but do not publish lot travelers, electrode masks, process recipes or implant factory qualification. The historical silicon-array paper is a fabrication comparator only.
steps.check: Accept packaged hardware as an external source. No exact base isolation, interconnects or coating process may be inferred from a historical 10 × 10 design.

steps.title: Inspect the separate arrays and cable assemblies
steps.detail: The paper describes four iridium-oxide-coated silicon grids connected by fine braided bundles to one titanium pedestal. A virtual package can represent each cable separately without implying a known wire order.
steps.check: Differentiate needle length from electrode count. The published needle length is 1.5 mm; the exposed conductive tip area is not given by that length.

steps.title: Build a bench-only hierarchical map
steps.detail: Assign every modeled site an (array,row,column) address and inject a known tag into a synthetic harness. Treat the actual pedestal/headstage pin table as missing unless independently provided.
steps.check: All 256 model addresses must be distinct. Passing a synthetic map does not validate the vendor pin assignment.

steps.title: Separate site-, bundle- and pedestal-level failure
steps.detail: Simulate a single open, loss of one 64-site bundle and common output loss as separate faults. If an impedance fixture is used, store electrolyte, frequency and reference. This is proposed bench QA, not a measurement reported at surgery.
steps.check: Expect 255, 192 and 0 available model electrodes under these idealized faults, respectively; no estimate of clinically usable channels follows.

gaps: No commercial master batch record, dose/clinical protocol, cable-to-pedestal pin table or per-site factory impedance thresholds are provided.
A patient-facing report is not manufacturing authorization, and the synthetic model does not predict patient performance.

sources.title: Wagner et al. (2026): TUM four-grid NeuroPort equipment
sources.note: Figure 1 and Methods identify four 8 × 8 Blackrock silicon arrays, 1.5 mm iridium-oxide-coated needles, braided connections and one titanium pedestal for each case. This is a configuration source, not a factory traveler.

sources.title: Jones et al. (1992): historical penetrating silicon array
sources.note: Academic design and fabrication comparator for planar arrays of penetrating silicon needles. This does not document the production steps, pinout, sizes or acceptance limits of the specific TUM apparatus.
